messages:
alex: heads-up — competitor just shipped 'adaptive-model-routing' in their hosted tier. saw a customer ping about it. anyone parsed the release notes yet?
mia: saw. lightweight: prioritizes latency by routing to smaller models when prompt < 128 tokens. basically an autoswitcher + cost cap.
sam: hmm. that sounds like our routing policies but more user-facing and automatic. customers will ask "why does their API feel cheaper for short chat"
jordan: agree. two paths: quick UX+opt-in shim that exposes an 'auto-route' flag, or build deeper metrics+rollback controls (longer). what are launch criteria for a safe quickship?
alex: minimal: 1) opt-in flag, 2) transparent audit logs showing route decisions, 3) cost/latency dashboard tile, 4) fallback to pinned model if mismatch. anything else?
mia: add: regression tests on quality for a few customer prompts (we have eval sets for support/comms). if any drop > 2% we block.
sam: dev effort estimate? eng estimates for opt-in path only?
jordan: rough: opt-in routing + audit logs = 2 wks eng + 3 days infra + 1 day QA. full rollout with metrics/auto-fallback is 6 wks.
alex: ask from sales: they want something in 2 weeks to reference in RFPs. can we scope the 2 week opt-in to avoid technical debt?
mia: scope it as 'experiment' behind feature-flag with auto-revert and cleanup ticket that must be closed before GA. also log all decisions + sample outputs to S3.
sam: noted. need product checklist: legal sign-off (audit logs), privacy check (no customer PII stored), SLA implications (does routing affect latency SLOs?).
jordan: I'll loop in legal & reliability. eng-bot: deployment queued: feature-flag branch built, canary tests scheduled at 1733333345.
alex: ok let's proceed with opt-in experiment. owners: jordan (pm), sam (eng), mia (data/quality). deliverable: opt-in flag + dashboard tile + eval run. ship target: 2 weeks.
mia: i'll prepare eval suite and a short quality gating doc.
sam: will add cleanup ticket to sprint board and include rollback playbook.
jordan: thanks. will post a one-pager for sales to use (limitations + metrics).
alex: perfect. @all please add any hard blockers within 24h. :thumbsup:
